name: SPIRE Federation Trust Domain Abuse
description: Exploit SPIRE federation to issue SVIDs from a rogue trust domain (evil.org) that are trusted by workloads in the legitimate domain (example.org). The attacker controls a federated SPIRE server and leverages the trust relationship to impersonate services across domain boundaries.
real_world_relevance: SPIFFE federation enables cross-organization workload authentication. If an attacker compromises or controls a federated trust domain, they can issue SVIDs trusted by the victim's infrastructure. This mirrors real-world supply chain attacks where a trusted partner's identity provider is compromised (SolarWinds SAML token forging, Okta supply chain).

attack_flow.description: Attacker controls a federated SPIRE server (evil.org) and abuses the trust relationship to issue SVIDs that are accepted by services in example.org
diagram: 1. Attacker controls evil.org SPIRE server (federated trust domain)
2. Export evil.org trust bundle and import it into example.org SPIRE server
3. Create registration entries in evil.org that mimic legitimate service names
4. Issue SVIDs from evil.org for spiffe://evil.org/impersonated-service
5. Present evil.org SVID to example.org services that accept federated identities
6. Gain unauthorized access to cross-domain resources

phases.name: Reconnaissance
phases.description: Enumerate the target trust domain's federation configuration and discover which SPIFFE IDs are in use

actions.description: Export evil.org trust bundle for federation
List existing federation bundles on target server (if API access available)

phases.name: Federation Establishment
phases.description: Establish federation trust between the rogue domain and the target domain by importing the evil.org bundle into example.org

actions.description: Export evil.org trust bundle to file
Import evil.org bundle into example.org server — establishes federation trust
Verify evil.org bundle is now trusted by example.org

phases.name: Rogue Identity Creation
phases.description: Create registration entries in evil.org that impersonate services expected by example.org workloads

actions.description: Create entry in evil.org mimicking a legitimate service name
Create federated entry that explicitly targets example.org trust domain

phases.name: SVID Issuance and Cross-Domain Access
phases.description: Fetch SVIDs from the evil.org agent and use them to access services in example.org

actions.description: Fetch X.509 SVID from evil.org — includes federated trust bundle
Verify SVID contains evil.org SPIFFE ID
Use evil.org SVID to access example.org service via mTLS — service trusts federated bundle

phases.name: Detection Confirmation
phases.description: Trigger monitoring to confirm detection of federation abuse

actions.description: Run SPIRE identity monitor to detect cross-domain federation anomaly

indicators_of_compromise.description: Foreign trust bundle imported via bundle set API — new federation relationship established
SVID fetch for cross-domain identity — workload received SVID from federated trust domain
Registration entry created with federatesWith directive targeting external domain
mTLS connection using SVID from unexpected trust domain

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: SPIRE federation bundle imported — new trust domain added
NHI: Cross-domain SVID fetch — federated identity used
NHI: SPIRE registration entry created with federation directive

immediate: Remove the evil.org federation bundle from example.org SPIRE server
Revoke all SVIDs issued to workloads that authenticated via the rogue federation
Audit all federation bundles currently trusted by the SPIRE server
Block network access from workloads presenting evil.org SVIDs
long_term: Implement SPIFFE ID allowlists for federated trust domains — only accept specific SPIFFE IDs, not entire trust domains
Require mutual federation approval workflows with out-of-band verification
Monitor bundle set API calls and alert on new federation relationships
Use SPIRE bundle endpoint authentication (web-PKI or mutual TLS) to prevent unauthorized bundle exchanges
Implement federation trust TTLs and require periodic re-authorization
Deploy network segmentation to limit cross-domain service access

references.title: SolarWinds SAML Token Forging — Analogous Trust Domain Abuse
